The Department of Mathematical Sciences at Carnegie Mellon University invites applications to our graduate program in Mathematics. To be admitted to this program applicants must document competence equivalent to graduation from a recognized U.S. four-year college, university or institute of technology. All Mathematics doctoral programs use the same application: the first question asks to specify the program.
There is no application fee.
All application materials should be received by December 20 to be assured of full consideration. Applications can be submitted after this date. But, we cannot guarantee that they will be reviewed by the Admissions Committee.
The following materials are required or optional (as indicated) as part of your application:
Curriculum Vitae
Statement of Purpose
Your statement of purpose should describe your mathematical background and interests, previous research experiences, as well as directions and goals you would like to pursue for your graduate studies. Information about your background or activities that helps identify your potential to grow and achieve will also be considered. Typical statements of purpose are about one or two pages long.
Transcripts
You need to submit transcripts from undergraduate and graduate programs you attended. Transcripts that are not in English should be submitted together with English translations. You may submit an unofficial transcript with your application; in this case official transcripts will be required later should you be accepted into the program.
Reference letters
You must submit contact information for at least three academic references. Your references will be directly asked to submit their letters of recommendation through this website.
Subject GRE score (optional)
We do not collect scores for the GRE General Test. The GRE Mathematics Subject Test is recommended but not required. Your application would receive full consideration without a score. You may submit an unofficial score with your application. If so, the official test report would be required later should you be accepted into the program.
Language Proficiency Test Scores (non-native English speakers)
All non-native English speakers must submit official language exam scores in order to receive consideration. If you are a non-native English speaker, you need to meet this requirement even if you attended a university in the U.S. No exceptions will be made.
We accept scores from the following language exams:
Duolingo English Test (DET)
Minimum cumulative score: 110/160
Recommended cumulative score: 120/160
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL)
Minimum cumulative score: 86/120
Recommended cumulative score: 100/120
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
Minimum cumulative score: 6.5
Recommended cumulative score: 7.5
Exam scores must be dated 2024 or later.
Unofficial or self-reported test scores are accepted at the time of application. But, we will not extend an offer of admission without official unexpired test scores.
This requirement exists to ensure your success at CMU as well as for university visa processing purposes should you be admitted.
